name: ProfMobius
milestone_by_age_26: Born November 23, 1980; co-founded Minecraft Mod Coder Pack (MCP) and later joined Mojang after Minecraft’s rise (~2010–2010s), when he was already ~29–35. Age 26 fell in 2006–2007, before Minecraft existed; no material, dated engineering/founder milestone by 26 found.
early_history_summary: Thomas “ProfMobius” Guimbretière is a French game developer known for co-founding MCP with Michael Stoyke (Searge), authoring popular mods (Waila, JABBA), then working as a Mojang Minecraft Java developer before leaving in 2020 for Razzleberries AB.
evidence_summary: Minecraft Wiki documents birth date November 23, 1980 and roles as MCP co-founder, mod author, and later Mojang developer (left June 2020). MCP and Minecraft modding post-date Minecraft’s 2009–2010 emergence, well after age 26. No independently verified material milestone by age 26 found.

name: Vicent Marti
milestone_by_age_26: In 2010 (age ~20), completed a GitHub-sponsored Google Summer of Code project to advance libgit2; by March 2011 GitHub hired him full-time as a GitHubber to maintain libgit2—the C library later powering core github.com Git operations—after open-source work that eliminated a technical interview.
early_history_summary: Born and raised in the Catalan Countries (~1990 per GitHub’s 2010 blog calling him a 20-year-old). As a university/master’s student he took on GSoC 2010 to “complete” libgit2 with GitHub mentor support, then contracted and joined GitHub full-time in March 2011, becoming a primary maintainer of libgit2 and later known for scaling Git at GitHub and open-source markdown (Sundown/Redcarpet).
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond origin in the Catalan Countries.
primary_early_advantage_tags: GSoC, libgit2, GitHub hire via OSS, systems C depth, open-source reputation
evidence_summary: GitHub’s November 2010 engineering blog described Vicent as a 20-year-old Catalan developer working toward a degree while building libgit2. Edward Thomson’s 2024 libgit2 history and Google Summer of Code archives confirm the 2010 GSoC sponsored by GitHub. GitHub’s March 29, 2011 “Vicent Marti is a GitHubber” post states he was hired full-time after contractor work following GSoC; Tom Preston-Werner separately noted the hire was based on open-source proof without a technical interview. Later work included maintaining libgit2, scaling Git at GitHub, and (as of 2025) engineering writing at PlanetScale.
starting_point: Born and raised in the Catalan Countries; university/master’s student in systems programming when he entered the Git open-source ecosystem via GSoC. Family background otherwise not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Engineer at PlanetScale (public technical posts on vector indexes and Go interpreters, 2025); former longtime GitHub engineer and libgit2 maintainer; open-source author of Redcarpet/Sundown-related work.

trajectory.event: Completed GitHub-sponsored Google Summer of Code on libgit2, turning a incomplete library into a modular, high-performance Git implementation target for github.com.
Hired full-time by GitHub (announced March 2011) as a GitHubber to maintain libgit2 and hard-core C systems work after contractor follow-on from GSoC.
Became a primary maintainer of libgit2; Tom Preston-Werner cited his OSS work as the sole hiring signal (no technical interview).
Continued leading libgit2 development used across GitHub’s platform and later adopted by other tooling ecosystems.
Publicly known for talks and work on scaling Git at GitHub (“My Mom Told Me That Git Doesn’t Scale” era infrastructure talks).
Publishing systems engineering work at PlanetScale (e.g., large vector indexes for relational databases; faster interpreters in Go).

name: Ben Silbermann
milestone_by_age_26: Born July 14, 1982; Pinterest development began December 2009 and closed beta launched March 2010, when he was 27. Worked at Google (online advertising) ~2006–2008 (ages ~24–26), but that employment is not a material founder/breakout milestone. No qualifying ≤26 milestone found; defining success arrived with Pinterest after age 26.
early_history_summary: Raised in Des Moines, Iowa by ophthalmologist parents; RSI at MIT (1998); Yale BA Political Science (2003); Google product/ad role 2006–2008; left to build iPhone apps (Tote failed), then co-founded Pinterest with Paul Sciarra and Evan Sharp.
family_context_summary: Parents Jane Wang and Neil Silbermann were ophthalmologists with a family practice in Urbandale/Des Moines, Iowa; Chinese and German descent.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were physicians (ophthalmology), not internet product or consumer tech operators; family hoped he might pursue medicine.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Pinterest IR confirm birth July 14, 1982, Yale 2003, Google 2006–2008, and Pinterest founding December 2009 / launch March 2010 at age 27. Multiple startup profiles list age at founding as 27. Pre-26 path is selective education plus ordinary big-tech employment; material product/company success is post-26.

name: Dan Larimer
milestone_by_age_26: AP News (March 2018) described him as a 35-year-old Virginia Tech graduate (implying birth ~1982–83; CSV lists 1981). Material blockchain milestones—BitShares/ProtoShares (~2013–2014), Steem (2016), EOS/Block.one (2017)—occurred in his early 30s. Age 26 was ~2007–2009: early software/entrepreneurship (e.g., Open Tech ~2005–2007) and later Bitcoin interest (2009) without a dated, material public breakthrough by 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Colorado; grew up in Virginia and Florida; Virginia Tech engineering/CS degree ~2003. Wrote software from childhood; serial entrepreneur since ~2004 (including Open Tech). Discovered bitcoin ~2009 while financially strained; later invented dPoS and founded BitShares, Steem, and co-built EOS as Block.one CTO.
family_context_summary: Father Stan Larimer was an aerospace engineer who later collaborated on blockchain consulting/Cryptonomex; AP reports periods of living with parents and financial strain around 2009.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father aerospace engineer with later blockchain involvement; not a documented early crypto/fintech apprenticeship before Larimer’s own breakthroughs.
evidence_summary: AP (2018) ages him at 35; BitcoinWiki and industry bios place VT graduation in 2003 and BitShares founding ~2013. Steem and EOS follow in 2016–2017. Early company stints pre-crypto are not independently documented as material public milestones by age 26. Career-defining crypto protocol work is clearly post-26.
